docs.title: RedLight Studio Kit
docs.text:
One-click studio lighting, backdrops, cameras and HDRIs for Blender.

RedLight Studio Kit puts a complete lighting studio in Blender's N-panel. Drop a rig on your model, pick a look from 60 studio kits, and render. Every light, backdrop and camera stays live and editable in the same panel.

  • :material-download: Installation: install, update, uninstall
  • :material-rocket-launch: Quick Start: a lit scene in under a minute
  • :material-lightbulb-group: Studio Kits: 60 looks in 7 categories
  • :material-format-list-bulleted: Kit List: every kit, with previews

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Add a rig. One controller holds every light, so the whole studio moves, rotates and scales together.
  2. Apply a kit. A kit sets the lights, the world colour and the backdrop colour in one click.
  3. Tune. Edit any light, swap the backdrop shape, add a camera or an HDRI, all without leaving the panel.

docs.title: What's included
docs.text:
• 60 studio kits: Product, Portrait, Dramatic, Colour Mood, Glass & Jewellery, Natural and Projection
  • 12 projection kits that use real shadow masks, so the patterns render in EEVEE and Cycles
  • 9 parametric backdrop shapes and a shadow-catcher floor
  • An inline light editor, quick light presets, Master and Exposure
  • Cameras with focal presets and depth of field
  • An HDRI browser for your own HDRI folder
  • Gobo images and 32 bundled IES profiles (Cycles)

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Blender 4.2 or newer. Tested on 4.5 LTS, 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2.
  • EEVEE or Cycles. See EEVEE & Cycles for the two features that need Cycles.
  • Windows, macOS or Linux.

docs.title: Backdrop
docs.text:
Open Backdrop, choose a shape and click Add. A rig has one backdrop. Applying a kit creates one for you if Set Backdrop is on.

Shape What it is L Curve (Cyclorama) Floor sweeping up into one back wall S Curve Floor stepping up to a raised plateau C Curve Floor, back wall and an overhanging ceiling Half Pipe Floor between two curved side walls Corner Back wall and side wall meeting at a sharp corner Curve Cove Back wall and side wall with a rounded corner Quarter Dome Half-dome shell wrapping behind the subject Half Dome Dome shell around the subject, open at the front Cylinder Stand Round product pedestal

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Shape dropdown switches shape. The new shape loads its own default sizes.
  • Size controls change with the shape: Width, Depth, Height, the curve radii, Wrap for the domes and Side for Corner and Curve Cove.
  • Segments sets how smooth the curves are.
  • The colour swatch and Roughness set the backdrop's material.
  • The trash icon removes the backdrop.

Everything stays editable after you add the backdrop.

docs.title: Floor
docs.text:
Open Floor, set Floor Size and click Add Shadow Catcher. The floor is invisible in the render except for the shadows that fall on it, so your model can sit on a transparent or HDRI background. It works in Cycles and EEVEE.

Note

The backdrop and floor do not follow Rig Transform. Use Fit Rig to Selection to move them under a model.

docs.title: Camera
docs.text: Button What it does Add Camera Adds a camera aimed at the rig and makes it the scene camera. Align Camera to View Moves the selected camera to match the current viewport view.

docs.title: The camera list
docs.text:
Every RedLight camera on the rig. Click a row to edit that camera. The camera icon on a row makes it the scene's active (render) camera.

Button What it does Minus Removes the selected camera. Refresh Rebuilds the list.

docs.title: Editing a camera
docs.text:
Control What it does Focal buttons One-click 24, 35, 50, 85 or 135 mm. Focal Length Any focal length. Depth of Field Turns depth of field on. F-Stop, Blades, Rotation, Ratio The aperture settings. Focus The object to focus on. The eyedropper sets it to the active object. Focus Distance Used when no focus object is set. Rotation, Location The camera's transform.

Cameras do not follow Rig Transform, so turning the rig changes the lighting without moving your framing.

First public release.

  • 60 studio kits in 7 categories, picked from a thumbnail grid.
  • Projection kits with real shadow masks, for EEVEE and Cycles.
  • Rig controller: move, rotate and scale the whole studio; Fit Rig to Selection; Master and Exposure.
  • 9 parametric backdrop shapes and a shadow-catcher floor.
  • Inline light editor with quick presets.
  • Cameras with focal presets and depth of field.
  • HDRI browser for your own folder.
  • Gobo images and 32 bundled IES profiles (Cycles).

docs.title: Custom Kits
docs.text: Kits are plain JSON files. Add your own and they show up in the grid.

docs.title: Where they go
docs.text:
Put a .json file in the add-on's kits folder, with a preview image named <kit id>.png next to it (256 x 256 works well). Restart Blender.

The folder is inside the installed add-on:

  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation\Blender\<version>\extensions\user_default\redlight_studio_kit\kits
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Blender/<version>/extensions/user_default/redlight_studio_kit/kits
  • Linux: ~/.config/blender/<version>/extensions/user_default/redlight_studio_kit/kits

Keep a copy

Updating or uninstalling the add-on replaces this folder. Keep your kit files somewhere else too and copy them back after an update.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
A file holds one kit, or a list of kits.

{
  "id": "MY_KIT",
  "name": "My Kit",
  "category": "PRODUCT",
  "description": "Key from the right, soft fill, cool rim",
  "target": [0, 0, 0.4],
  "world": {"color": [0.02, 0.02, 0.02], "strength": 1.0},
  "backdrop": {"shape": "L_CURVE", "color": [0.2, 0.2, 0.2], "roughness": 0.6},
  "lights": [
    {"role": "KEY", "type": "AREA", "pos": [3, -3, 2.7], "energy": 650,
     "size": 2.0, "size_y": 1.5, "shape": "RECTANGLE", "color": [1, 1, 1]},
    {"role": "FILL", "type": "AREA", "pos": [-3, -2.4, 1.5], "energy": 260,
     "size": 2.8, "temperature": 7000},
    {"role": "RIM", "type": "SPOT", "pos": [0, 3, 3], "energy": 800,
     "spot_size": 25, "spot_blend": 0.3, "radius": 0.05}
  ]
}

Only id, lights and each light's type, pos and energy are required.

docs.title: Kit fields
docs.text: Field Meaning id Unique id, also the preview file name. name, description Shown in the grid and under the thumbnail. category PRODUCT, PORTRAIT, DRAMATIC, COLOR, GLASS, NATURAL or PATTERN (Projection). target The point lights aim at, unless a light sets its own. Default [0, 0, 0.4]. world World color and strength. backdrop shape, color, roughness. The shape is only used when the rig has no backdrop yet.

docs.title: Light fields
docs.text:
Field Applies to Meaning type all AREA, SPOT, SUN or POINT pos all Position in metres, relative to the rig energy all Watts (Sun: W/m2) role all KEY, FILL, RIM, BACK or TOP name all Object name color all Linear RGB temperature all Kelvin target all Aim point for this light size, size_y, shape, spread Area Size in metres; RECTANGLE, SQUARE, DISK or ELLIPSE; spread in degrees spot_size, spot_blend, radius Spot Cone in degrees, edge blend, source radius radius Point Source radius angle Sun Angular size in degrees mask Spot A projection mask, see below

Author kits for a subject about 1 m tall at rig scale 1.

docs.title: Projection masks
docs.text:
Add a mask to a spot light to project a pattern:

{"type": "SPOT", "pos": [-3, -2, 4], "energy": 1800, "spot_size": 80,
 "radius": 0.015, "target": [0, 1, 0],
 "mask": {"pattern": "blinds", "twist": 0}}

pattern is one of blinds, window, lattice, slash, foliage, checker, pinholes or bars. twist rotates the pattern, in degrees. Use a small radius (0.015) for crisp edges and about 0.05 for foliage.

docs.title: Does it work in EEVEE?
docs.text: Yes. Every kit, including the projection patterns, renders in EEVEE and Cycles. Gobo images and IES profiles need Cycles. See EEVEE & Cycles.

docs.title: Which Blender versions are supported?
docs.text: Blender 4.2 and newer. It is tested on 4.5 LTS, 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2.

docs.title: Will applying a kit delete my own lights?
docs.text: No. A swap only replaces lights that came from a kit. Lights you added with Add Light stay, and so do the floor and cameras.

docs.title: My model is huge or tiny. Will the kits still work?
docs.text: Yes. Select the model and click Fit Rig to Selection. The studio is scaled to the model and light power is adjusted so the look stays the same.

docs.title: Some kits lose shadows in EEVEE. Why?
docs.text: Kits with many lights can fill EEVEE's shadow memory. Raise Render Properties > Shadows > Pool Size to 1024 MB. Cycles is not affected.

docs.title: I can't see the lights in my render. Is that right?
docs.text: Yes. RedLight's lights are hidden from the camera on purpose. They still light the scene and appear in reflections.

docs.title: Rig Transform doesn't move my floor or backdrop.
docs.text: That is by design, so you can sweep the lighting around a fixed set. Use Fit Rig to Selection to move the floor and backdrop under a model.

docs.title: My gobo or IES has no effect.
docs.text: Check the render engine. Both need Cycles. Also check that the light named at the top of the Light Texture section is the one you meant.

docs.title: Are HDRIs included?
docs.text: The HDRI browser works with your own HDRI folder. None are bundled in version 1.0. 32 IES profiles are included.

docs.title: Can I make my own kits?
docs.text: Yes. See Custom Kits.

docs.title: Do I need the license key?
docs.text: No. The add-on works without it. The key identifies your order when you ask for support.

docs.title: I had LuxKit installed. Anything to do?
docs.text: Uninstall LuxKit before installing RedLight Studio Kit. They cannot be enabled together. Rigs made with LuxKit keep working.

docs.title: HDRI
docs.text: The HDRI section lights the scene with an environment map from your own folder.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > RedLight Studio Kit.
  2. Set HDRI Folder to a folder of .hdr or .exr files.
  3. Back in the panel, open HDRI and click Refresh.

RedLight builds a thumbnail for each file the first time it sees it, so a large folder takes a moment on the first refresh.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control What it does Thumbnail grid Click to pick an HDRI. It is applied to the world straight away. Strength Environment brightness. Rotation Turns the environment around the vertical axis. Refresh Rescans the folder. Clear Removes the RedLight environment from the world.

Keeping your HDRI when applying kits

A kit normally sets a solid world colour, which replaces the HDRI. Turn off Set World in Studio Kits to keep it.

No HDRIs are bundled in version 1.0.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Blender 4.2 or newer.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Install the zip file. Do not unzip it into Blender's folders by hand: a hand-copied folder has no Uninstall button and can misbehave.

Easiest:

  1. Drag redlight_studio_kit-x.x.x.zip onto the Blender window.
  2. Confirm the install prompt.

Or:

  1. Edit > Preferences > Add-ons.
  2. Open the dropdown in the top-right corner and choose Install from Disk...
  3. Pick redlight_studio_kit-x.x.x.zip.
  4. Tick the checkbox next to RedLight Studio Kit.

The panel appears in the 3D Viewport sidebar. Press N and open the RedLight tab.

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Install the new zip the same way, over the top. Blender replaces the old version. Rigs in your existing files keep working.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
1. Edit > Preferences > Add-ons.
  2. Find RedLight Studio Kit and expand its row.
  3. Click Uninstall.
No Uninstall button?

The add-on was copied onto disk by hand instead of installed from the zip. Untick it in Preferences, quit Blender, then delete this folder (<version> is your Blender version, for example 4.5):

  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation\Blender\<version>\extensions\user_default\redlight_studio_kit
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Blender/<version>/extensions/user_default/redlight_studio_kit
  • Linux: ~/.config/blender/<version>/extensions/user_default/redlight_studio_kit

docs.title: Optional setup
docs.text:
In Preferences > Add-ons > RedLight Studio Kit you can set:

Setting What it does HDRI Folder A folder of .hdr / .exr files. They appear in the HDRI grid. Gobo / IES Folder A folder of gobo images and .ies profiles. They appear in the Gobo & IES grids next to the 32 bundled IES profiles. License Key Optional. It identifies your order for support. The add-on works without it.

docs.title: The Panel
docs.text: RedLight lives in the 3D Viewport sidebar (N) under the RedLight tab.

docs.title: Header
docs.text: The logo, the product name and the installed version.

docs.title: Rig
docs.text:
Control What it does Rig The rig the panel is editing. Pick another rig here if the scene has several. Add Rig Creates a new rig at the world origin. Trash icon Removes the active rig with its lights, floor, backdrop and cameras. Fit Rig to Selection Moves the studio under the selected object and scales it to fit. Needs a selected object.

See The Rig.

docs.title: Master and Exposure
docs.text:
Control What it does Master Dims or brightens every rig light together, in stops (-10 to +10). It changes each light's Power, keeping their balance. Exposure Sets Blender's own per-light Exposure value on every rig light, in stops.

New lights and newly applied kits pick up both values.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Each section opens and closes with the arrow next to its name.

Section Page Rig Transform (whole studio) The Rig Lights Lights Light Texture (Gobo / IES) Gobo & IES Studio Kits Studio Kits Backdrop, Floor Backdrops & Floor Camera Camera HDRI HDRI

Rig Transform only appears once a rig exists.

docs.title: Studio Kits
docs.text: A kit is a complete look: the lights, the world colour and the backdrop colour. RedLight ships 60 of them in 7 categories.

docs.title: Applying a kit
docs.text:
1. Open Studio Kits.
  2. Choose a category in the dropdown, or leave it on All Kits.
  3. Click the thumbnail to open the grid and pick a kit. Its description appears under the thumbnail.
  4. Click Apply Kit.

docs.title: What a swap keeps
docs.text:
Applying a kit replaces only the lights that came from a kit. It keeps:

  • lights you added with Add Light,
  • the floor and cameras,
  • your backdrop's shape and size (only its colour changes).

docs.title: Set World and Set Backdrop
docs.text:
Two toggles under Apply Kit, both on by default.

Toggle On Off Set World The kit sets the world (background) colour. This replaces a RedLight HDRI. Your world is left alone. Use this to keep an HDRI. Set Backdrop The kit sets the backdrop colour, and creates its backdrop if the rig has none. No backdrop is created or recoloured.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Category Kits For Product 5 Clean, even light for products and packshots Portrait 5 Classic portrait patterns for characters and busts Dramatic 10 Low-key, hard-light and stage looks Colour Mood 12 Coloured gels, tinted sets and coloured shadows Glass & Jewellery 11 Edge strips and shaped reflections for glossy surfaces Natural 5 Sun, sky and window looks Projection 12 Patterns: blinds, windows, grids, dapple, scanlines

Every kit is listed with its preview in the Kit List.

docs.title: Projection kits
docs.text:
Projection kits throw a pattern across the scene. Each one places a black mask with holes in it in front of a spot light, so the pattern is a real shadow. That is why they work in EEVEE as well as Cycles.

  • The mask is parented to its light. Move or aim the light and the pattern follows.
  • The mask cannot be selected in the viewport, so you can't knock it out of place. It is hidden from the camera.
  • Deleting the light, or swapping the kit, removes its mask.
  • A larger Radius on the light gives softer pattern edges.

docs.title: Gobo & IES
docs.text:
The Light Texture (Gobo / IES) section shapes the beam of a single light.

Cycles only

Gobo images and IES profiles only render in Cycles. EEVEE ignores them, and the panel shows a warning when the render engine is not Cycles. For patterns in EEVEE, use the Projection studio kits.

docs.title: Which light?
docs.text: The section acts on the selected light: the active light in the viewport, or the highlighted row in the Lights list. Its name is shown at the top. To texture several lights, select each one and click Apply again.

docs.title: Gobo image
docs.text:
A gobo projects an image through the light, like a slide. It works best on a Spot light.

  1. Set Gobo / IES Folder in the add-on preferences to a folder of images (.png, .jpg, .tif, .tga, .bmp). White lets light through, black blocks it.
  2. Click Refresh, pick an image in the grid and click Apply Gobo.
  3. Scale and Rotation adjust the projection.

No gobo images are bundled in version 1.0.

docs.title: IES profile
docs.text:
An IES profile gives a light the real spread pattern of a physical fixture. It suits Spot and Point lights.

  1. Pick a profile in the grid. 32 profiles are bundled.
  2. Click Apply IES.

Your own .ies files in the Gobo / IES Folder appear in the same grid.

docs.title: Clear
docs.text: Clear removes the gobo or IES from the selected light.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text: The bundled profiles are the IES Lights Pack by LeoMoon, GPL-3.0, redistributed unmodified.

docs.title: Adding a light
docs.text: Choose a type (Area, Spot, Sun or Point) and click Add Light. The light joins the active rig, aimed at its centre. Lights you add this way survive kit swaps.

docs.title: The light list
docs.text:
Every light on the rig, with its role (Key, Fill, Rim, Back, Top). Click a row to edit that light. Selecting a light in the viewport or Outliner works too.

Button What it does Minus Removes the selected light. Refresh Rebuilds the list, for example after you delete a light in the Outliner. Trash Deletes every light on the rig. The floor stays.

docs.title: Editing a light
docs.text:
The box under the list edits the selected light directly.

Control Applies to Power, colour All lights Use Temperature, Temperature (Kelvin) All lights (Blender 4.3 and newer) Shape, Size X, Size Y Area Cone, Blend Spot Angle Sun Radius Point Rotation, Location All lights (a Sun only uses rotation)

docs.title: Light presets
docs.text:
Pick a preset in the dropdown at the bottom of the editor and click Apply. It sets the selected light's power, colour, size and temperature.

Preset Look Soft Key Broad, neutral key Hard Key Small, punchy key with crisp shadows Cool Fill Low, cool fill Warm Rim Warm separation light Golden Hour Warm, low-temperature wash

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• RedLight's lights are hidden from the camera. They light the scene and show in reflections, but the light itself never appears in the render.
  • Master and Exposure at the top of the panel act on every rig light at once. See The Panel.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
A lit, framed scene in under a minute.

  1. Open the 3D Viewport sidebar (N) and click the RedLight tab.
  2. Select your model and click Fit Rig to Selection. This creates a rig, moves it under the model and sizes the studio to fit.
  3. Open Studio Kits, click the thumbnail and pick a kit. Use the category dropdown above it to narrow the grid.
  4. Click Apply Kit. The lights, world colour and backdrop appear.
  5. Switch the viewport to Rendered to see the result.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Try another kit. Swapping replaces only the kit's lights; anything you added yourself stays.
  • Dim or brighten everything with Master.
  • Change the backdrop shape in Backdrops & Floor.
  • Add a camera in Camera.
  • Edit one light in Lights.

No model selected?

You can skip step 2. Apply Kit creates a rig at the world origin if the scene has none. Kits are sized for a subject about 1 m tall.

docs.title: EEVEE & Cycles
docs.text:
RedLight works in both render engines. Two features need Cycles, and EEVEE has one setting worth knowing about.

Feature EEVEE Cycles All 60 studio kits Yes Yes Projection kits (pattern masks) Yes Yes Backdrops, shadow-catcher floor Yes Yes Cameras, HDRI Yes Yes Gobo images No Yes IES profiles No Yes

Gobo images and IES profiles rely on light textures, which EEVEE does not support. That is a Blender limitation. The panel warns you when the engine is not Cycles.

docs.title: Missing shadows in EEVEE
docs.text:
Kits with many lights, such as Ring Catchlight (12 lights), can fill EEVEE's shadow memory. EEVEE then drops shadows without an error in the interface; the console prints Shadow buffer full.

Fix: Render Properties > Shadows > Pool Size, raise it to 1024 MB.

docs.title: Looks differ slightly between engines
docs.text: Cycles traces bounced light, so a brightly lit floor lifts the walls around it. EEVEE approximates this, so the same kit can look a little darker in the shadows. Turning on Render Properties > Raytracing in EEVEE brings the two closer.

docs.title: The Rig
docs.text: A rig is one controller (an Empty) with every light parented to it. Move, rotate or scale the controller and the whole studio follows.

docs.title: Creating and removing
docs.text:
• Add Rig creates a rig at the world origin.
  • Apply Kit, Add Light and Fit Rig to Selection create one for you if the scene has none.
  • The trash icon next to Add Rig removes the active rig and everything it made: lights, floor, backdrop and cameras.

A scene can hold several rigs. The Rig field at the top of the panel chooses which one you are editing.

docs.title: Fit Rig to Selection
docs.text:
Select your model and click Fit Rig to Selection. RedLight:

  1. moves the rig to the base of the model,
  2. scales the studio to the model's size,
  3. moves the floor and backdrop to match,
  4. adjusts light power so the exposure stays the same.

Kits are authored for a subject about 1 m tall, so this is how you light something much bigger or smaller with the same look.

docs.title: Rig Transform
docs.text:
Control What it does Location, Rotation Move and turn the whole studio. Scale Scales the whole studio. Light power follows, so a bigger studio is not darker. Reset Transform Back to the world origin, no rotation, scale 1.

The floor and backdrop stay put

Rig Transform moves the lights only. The floor, backdrop and cameras are not parented to the rig, so rotating the rig sweeps the light around a fixed set. Fit Rig to Selection is the tool that moves them.
